name: Magnetohydrodynamic Shear Pistol MHSP-2 'Riptide'
description: The MHSP-2 generates a directed magnetohydrodynamic field that interacts violently with the conductive saline content of biological tissue. When the field engages a target, it induces opposing directional currents through fluid-dense regions — primarily muscle bellies, joint capsules, and organ tissue — creating a shearing force that tears tissue longitudinally without penetrating the skin. The effect is functionally similar to a severe internal strain injury distributed across a limb or torso segment in under a tenth of a second.
specifications:
length: 29 cm
weight: 1.6 kg
power source: Zheng-Dao ZD-Flux cell (compact MHD)
effective range: 4–35 m
field aperture: Variable, 15–40 cm diameter at target
discharge rate: Semi-automatic, 0.8 second recycle
shots per cell: 34
housing: Polymer-ceramic composite, field-isolated grip
tactical_use: The MHSP-2 is a compliance and incapacitation weapon when operated at standard settings, capable of dropping a target by destroying muscular cohesion in a limb without lethal injury. At maximum aperture compression, operators can concentrate the shear field to rupture deep connective tissue and cause joint dislocation. Security teams use it for non-lethal extraction of high-value targets where physical integrity matters. Closed-field operators — bodyguards, detention specialists — carry it as a primary sidearm in environments where projectile weapons are scannable but energy sidearms require higher licensing.
cultural_context: Zheng-Dao Bioelectric markets the MHSP-2 openly to licensed security contractors as a 'humane restraint solution,' and its presence on a guard's hip is a status signal — it says the carrier works for someone who wants live captives, not corpses. In Meridian 88's debt-collection economy, MHSP-2 operators are called 'pullers' — a term that has drifted from the weapon's physics to a professional designation. The weapon is also common in underground fighting arenas where promoters want dramatic incapacitations rather than deaths.
story_hooks: A series of kidnappings in the financial district share a signature — victims are found with characteristic internal shear injuries but no external marks, suggesting MHSP-2 use by a highly organized extraction team.

A licensed 'puller' approaches the party for help: their MHSP-2 was remotely bricked mid-contract by Zheng-Dao, stranding them in a hostile situation — and now they want to know why the manufacturer killed their weapon.
An underground fight promoter is running MHSP-2-equipped enforcers to rig bouts, and a fighter who survived an 'accidental' incapacitation wants justice.
Zheng-Dao Bioelectric is quietly recalling a batch of MHSP-2 units with a firmware anomaly that causes the shear field to invert — instead of pulling tissue apart, it compresses it catastrophically.
